subject: Urgent: LedgerWave sustained 95th pct latency spike — exec sync requested
messages:
From: Janelle Park <janelle.park@ledgerwave.com>
To: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: account-support@ledgerwave.com
Date: 2026-11-07T06:58:00Z
Subject: Impacting: API latency & 5xx rate up since 06:45 UTC

Vivek / Marissa —

We started seeing a sustained spike in 95th percentile latency and a rising 5xx rate across our Checkout API at ~06:45 UTC. Error rate climbed from ~0.2% to 6.8% and p95 latency jumped from 180ms to ~1.6s. This is impacting live traffic.

What we observed: 
- Spike started ~06:45 UTC and is ongoing
- Affected endpoints: /v1/checkout/* across multiple regions (us-west, us-east)
- Sample request IDs attached in latency_logs_20261107.zip

We escalated internally and are pausing a small percentage of traffic, but we need Redwood to triage — this looks like network path/peering or DNS anomalies on your side (we see long DNS resolution times from your edge). Can you confirm?

Please advise immediate mitigation and ETA. We need an exec-level sync if unblocking isn’t fast.

Thanks,
Janelle Park
SRE Lead, LedgerWave

Attachments: latency_logs_20261107.zip
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Janelle Park <janelle.park@ledgerwave.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-07T07:03:00Z

Janelle — thanks for the alert and the logs. We see the ticket and are treating as P1.

Immediate items we are doing now: 
- Engineering (rishi) and network oncall are looking at VPC peering metrics and DNS latencies.
- I've asked infra to provision an alternate peering path and start a failover test to reduce RTT for affected edge nodes.
- Can you share 2-3 full request IDs that still show >1s latency (we'll correlate at our edge)?

We’ll update within 30 minutes or sooner if we have a mitigation. If we can't resolve quickly, we will schedule an executive bridge — marissa, can you prep a short exec one-pager?

— Vivek

Lauren / Michael —

Quick summary: LedgerWave reporting broad p95 latency and 5xx increase starting 06:45 UTC. External SRE suspects DNS/peering. Engineering is investigating; network is attempting an alternate-peering failover.

Why exec: customer is revenue-critical and is asking for exec-level updates; they have paused some traffic. I recommend a 30-minute exec sync at 10:30 PT (13:30 ET) to review mitigation and next steps.

Attaching a one-pager I'm drafting (exec-sync-agenda.pdf). Vivek will lead the bridge; Rishi will have technical notes.

Marissa

Attachments: exec-sync-agenda.pdf
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, michael_grant@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-07T08:01:00Z
Subject: Initial triage: VPC peering + DNS RTT anomalies (notes)

Quick technical notes from network triage (observed 07:00–07:50 UTC):
- BGP flaps observed on peer-id 192.0.2.14 affecting three edge POPs; intermittently changed preferred path which increased RTT by 200–1200ms.
- DNS resolution count from our edges to LedgerWave authoritative nameservers spiked with timeouts; median DNS RTT went from ~30ms to ~420ms for those POPs.
- Packet captures attached (route-trace-06_45.pcap) show retransmits and delayed ACKs between our edge and the peering fabric.

Mitigations underway: 
1) Configured fast failover to alternate peering fabric for affected POPs (in progress).
2) Dropped concurrent prefetches to reduce burstiness at ingress for LedgerWave routes.
3) Working with our cloud provider to stabilize BGP session — they confirm an upstream maintenance window on a subset of transit routers (unplanned).

Next: if failover completes cleanly, we'll monitor p95 and 5xx for 30–60 minutes and then propose follow-up RCA and permanent peering adjustments. If failover fails or oscillates, we will escalate to exec and propose capacity reservation on a dedicated egress pool.

— Rishi
Sr. Network Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: route-trace-06_45.pcap
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Janelle Park <janelle.park@ledgerwave.com>, Adam Chen <adam.chen@ledgerwave.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-07T09:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Impacting: API latency & 5xx rate up since 06:45 UTC

On Sat, Nov 7, 2026 at 06:58 AM Janelle Park <janelle.park@ledgerwave.com> wrote:
> Vivek / Marissa —
> 
> We started seeing a sustained spike in 95th percentile latency and a rising 5xx rate across our Checkout API at ~06:45 UTC....

Janelle — thanks for the quick heads up and logs. Update: 
- We completed an automated failover for the affected POPs to an alternate peering fabric at 08:32 UTC — initial telemetry shows p95 dropping from ~1.6s to ~240ms and 5xx rate moving down toward baseline.
- We also temporarily limited per-connection prefetches toward LedgerWave routes which reduced in-flight bursts.
- Cloud provider reported an unplanned transit router maintenance that likely triggered BGP instability; they are opening an incident with their network ops.

Immediate ask of LedgerWave: please keep a small traffic slice paused for 30–60 minutes while we watch for oscillation. If you can share 3 live request IDs with current p95 > 1s, we'll correlate through our edge logs (we tried matching your attached IDs but need a few live samples).

If p95 and 5xx do not stay stable, we will run an exec bridge at 10:30 PT (13:30 ET). I will join that bridge along with Rishi and our cloud network contact.

Appreciate the quick collaboration — will update in 15.

— Vivek
VP, Customer Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: executive-ops@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-07T11:20:00Z
Subject: Exec update: LedgerWave mitigation & next steps

Folks —

Short update for execs after the initial mitigation: 
- What happened: Unplanned upstream transit maintenance produced BGP instability and elevated DNS RTTs for several POPs leading to p95 spikes and increased 5xx at LedgerWave.
- What we did: Triggered automated alternate-peering failover, throttled connection prefetching, and engaged cloud provider NOC. Initial metrics show recovery trends (p95 back near 200–300ms in affected POPs).
- Risk / next steps: If transit instability recurs we will propose: (A) reserve dedicated egress capacity for LedgerWave for next 72 hrs, or (B) reconfigure permanent multi-homing across partners. Both options require approvals (cost + ops).

Action items: 
1) Marissa: prepare customer exec note and propose compensation language if LedgerWave remains impacted (estimate options).
2) Michael: confirm cost/feasibility for 72-hr dedicated egress reservation and earliest ETA.
3) Rishi: complete RCA draft with packet captures and TTL timelines.

We will hold the exec sync at 10:30 PT only if recovery regresses; otherwise we'll send a status note to LedgerWave and keep monitoring.

Lauren Bishop
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
